answers.note: A complete, well-sequenced 12-lesson plan with named retrieval starters, two checkpoint lessons before the assessment and an assessment that matches the content taught.

The lesson order and see-modify-make approach are sound, but lessons list a focus rather than objectives, retrieval and checkpoints are only mentioned in passing, and the assessment timing (15 + 35 minutes plus 5 minutes of testing) overruns the 50-minute lesson.

The table is clear and each starter draws on earlier lessons, but while loops are never taught, so the Lesson 11 guessing game outruns the content; the only real checkpoint comes in Lesson 10, and the tasks lean heavily on guided typing.

The solutions are correct and the stretch tasks are rich, but students go straight to writing code after one predict task, the debugging task (with an infinite loop) is hidden in an optional extension, and there are few test cases or hints.

A well-graded predict-trace-modify-make sequence with a debugging task covering both an infinite loop and an off-by-one error, a full test-case table, staged hints, challenges and correct solutions (including the 27-day doubling answer).

The progression is clear and the debugging task with planted infinite-loop and off-by-one bugs works well, but only Task 5 has test cases, the Task 2 trace table is printed already filled in, and the only stretch is a one-line extension with no solution.

Clear script, timings, answer key and collection instructions, but about 20 short recall questions are stretched across 45 minutes, leaving too little real work and only a 3-minute slot for the challenge.

A solid, non-specialist-friendly lesson (draw and label, organ jobs table, sandwich journey, challenge, read-aloud quiz) with full answers and clear instructions to leave the books or sheets on the desk.

A very thorough pack with a word-for-word script, timings, a quiz, a scaffolded writing frame, challenge and exit question, full answers with model responses, and explicit hand-in and absence notes, though Q9 is awkwardly worded.
